label: Retained readings from New Testament, John
summary: 8.58: The Abraham saying is used in docs/john-abraham-saying.md to compare a divine self-identification with weaker readings. A case link requires a defended interpretation of the reported formula in context and a report-to-event bridge. 8.59: The stone-taking report constrains interpretation in docs/john-abraham-saying.md. The reaction alone does not identify what the interlocutors took the saying to mean. Applying it to a claim of divine authority requires a bridge from the reported reaction to its motive and the meaning of the saying. 9.8-9: The blind man's self-identification serves as a lexical control in docs/john-abraham-saying.md. It defeats a reading rule based on the words alone, but application to John 8 needs an argument about the different context and the force of the whole utterance.
